args.name: weekly review
steps: summarize_notes

skills.name: Audit link reasons
skills.description: Rewrites vague 'similar in meaning' links into specific reasons.
skills.when_to_use: When I ask you to clean up or audit my links, or when the graph feels too vague.
skills.prompt: Audit the graph for links that have vague reasons (like 'similar in meaning') and rewrite them to be more accurate based on the notes' contents.
steps: Run the audit_link_reasons tool to process a batch of vague links.
Report back how many links were updated.

skills.name: Find where I disagreed with myself
skills.description: Reads related notes and reports the ones that can't both be right.
skills.when_to_use: When I ask what I changed my mind about, whether my notes are consistent, or where I contradicted myself.
skills.prompt: Look for places where my own notes contradict each other, a decision I reversed, a date that moved, a view I changed, and tell me what you found.
steps: Run the find_contradictions tool.
For each one, say what the two notes claim and how far apart they were written: the gap is the point, since the interesting case is a change of mind rather than a slip.
Do NOT link anything on your own. Offer to link the ones I agree with, and only then use link_notes with link_type 'contradicts'.
If nothing was found, say so plainly rather than reaching for a weak example: a wrong accusation is worse here than no answer.

skills.name: Notebook health check
skills.description: A full audit: reports what needs fixing, changes nothing.
skills.when_to_use: before a clean-up, or when the notebook feels disorganised
skills.prompt: Audit my whole notebook and report what needs attention. Do NOT change anything: this is a report, not a clean-up.
steps: Get the notebook's overview: categories, tags and the total note count: in one notebook_overview call.
Name the categories that are nearly empty, and any that hold so much they are not really sorting anything.
Name the tags that look like duplicates of each other (singular and plural, different spellings, near-synonyms).
List a sample of the notes sitting in Uncategorised.
Say what those Uncategorised notes are actually about, so I can see which categories are missing.
Finish with a short numbered list of what to fix, worst first, naming which of the clean-up skills would fix each one. Remind me you changed nothing.

skills.name: Clean up my tags
skills.description: Merges duplicate tags and removes ones that don't fit.
skills.when_to_use: when tags have drifted, plurals, synonyms, one-offs
skills.prompt: Go through my tags, merge the duplicates, and remove the ones that don't fit.
steps: List every tag I use, with its count.
Group the tags that mean the same thing, singular and plural, different spellings, near-synonyms, and pick the best name for each group.
Merge each group with rename_tag, onto the name you picked; renaming a tag onto an existing one merges them. If you found no duplicates, say so and move on.
List the notes whose tags may not match what they actually say, so you have something to check.
Read each of those notes in full with get_note before judging its tags.
Use tag_note to remove the tags that do not fit. If they all fit, say so rather than removing something to look busy.
Use tag_note to add better tags where a note is under-tagged.
Tell me every change you made, grouped by what kind it was.

skills.name: Reorganise my categories
skills.description: Proposes a category structure, then moves notes into it.
skills.when_to_use: when Uncategorised is full or categories have stopped fitting
skills.prompt: Reorganise my categories so they actually fit what I write about.
steps: List my categories with their counts.
Read a sample of notes from the biggest category and from Uncategorised.
Tell me the structure you propose, which categories to add, which to rename, which to merge, and why, before changing anything.
Create the categories you proposed with create_category. If you proposed none, say so.
Rename the categories whose names no longer fit, with rename_category.
Merge the categories that are really the same thing, with merge_categories.
Read a note with get_note before deciding where it belongs, the choice has to be based on what it says.
Move each note into the right category with edit_note: one call per note.
Tell me what you changed and how many notes moved.

skills.name: Fix my links
skills.description: Removes connections that don't hold up, and adds ones that should exist.
skills.when_to_use: when the graph has links that no longer make sense
skills.prompt: Check the links between my notes: remove the ones that don't hold up, add the ones that should be there.
steps: Call list_notes to see what is in the notebook.
Call related_notes on one of the notes that came back, to see what it links to and how. If it comes back with no links, call it again on a different one.
Call get_note on each note at the other end of those links: one call per note, starting with the first.
Say which of those links genuinely belong together and which do not, with a reason for each.
Use unlink_notes on the ones that do not hold up. If they all hold up, say so rather than removing one anyway.
Use related_notes with include_suggestions to find notes that read alike but were never linked.
Read those pairs with get_note, a similar score is a hint, not a reason.
Use link_notes only where the connection is real.
Report what you unlinked and what you linked, with the reason for each.

skills.name: Find notes worth combining
skills.description: Spots fragments and duplicates that should be one note. Reports only.
skills.when_to_use: when the same thing has been written down several times
skills.prompt: Find notes that are really the same thing written more than once, and show me what combining them would look like. Do not merge or delete anything yourself.
steps: Call list_notes to see what is in the notebook.
Call related_notes with include_suggestions on a few of those notes, to find ones that read alike but were never linked.
Read each candidate pair or group in full with get_note, a similar score is a hint and is often wrong.
For each group that is genuinely the same thing, show me the combined note you would write, with the note ids it came from.
Link the members of each group together with link_notes, so they are easy to find again.
Tell me you have not deleted or merged anything.

skills.name: Summarise my week
skills.description: The last seven days, in a paragraph.
skills.prompt: Summarise what I saved in the last 7 days.
steps: Find the notes I saved in the last 7 days.
Read the ones that look substantial with get_note, rather than working from the previews.
Write the summary: the main topics, anything that looks important, and one thing worth revisiting.

skills.name: Find loose ends
skills.description: Unfinished things you wrote down and left.
skills.prompt: Find the loose ends in my notes and list them.
steps: Go through my notes page by page with list_notes, and keep going until it says there are no more. Note which ones read as unfinished: todo, need to, should, waiting on, must, chase up, follow up.
Read each candidate with get_note, to check it is genuinely unfinished rather than something I already closed off.
List each loose end with its note id, newest first.

skills.name: Auto-tag my notes
skills.description: Adds 2–3 tags to notes that have none.
skills.prompt: Tag the notes in my notebook that have no tags yet.
steps: List the tags I already use, so new ones match rather than duplicate them.
Find my notes with no tags, or only one.
Read each of those notes with get_note, so the tags describe what it actually says.
Call tag_note on each of those notes with 2–3 short, reusable tags.
Tell me which notes you tagged, and with what.

skills.name: Link related notes
skills.description: Connects notes that are clearly about the same thing.
skills.prompt: Connect the notes in my notebook that belong together.
steps: Look through my notes for pairs that are clearly about the same thing but aren't linked yet.
Read both notes of a pair with get_note before deciding, a shared word is not a shared subject.
Link each pair you are confident about with link_notes.
Give me a short summary of what you connected, and why.

skills.name: Tidy suggestions
skills.description: Proposes tidy-ups. Changes nothing on its own.
skills.prompt: Suggest how I could tidy my notebook, without changing it.
steps: Get the notebook's overview, categories, tags and totals, in one notebook_overview call.
Find the overlaps: tags that mean the same thing, categories with one or two notes, notes that look misfiled.
Give me the suggestions as a numbered list and ask which ones I want applied. Do not change anything yourself.

skills.name: Catch up on a topic
skills.description: Everything you've written about one thing.
skills.prompt: Pull together everything I have written about {{topic}}.
steps: Search my notes for {{topic}}.
Read the most relevant ones in full with get_note.
Tell me what I seem to think about {{topic}}, what is still unresolved, and what I said about it most recently.

skills.name: Write a document from a tag
skills.description: Every note under one tag, written up as one document.
skills.prompt: Write one document that brings together every note I tagged {{tag}}.
steps: List the notes tagged {{tag}}.
Read each one in full with get_note, rather than working from the previews.
Decide the order the notes read best in, and what the document should open with. Do not invent anything the notes do not say.
Save it with create_document, titled after {{tag}}, as Markdown with a heading for each theme, and say which notes it draws on.

skills.name: Daily review
skills.description: Today's notes, turned into tomorrow's list.
skills.prompt: Review what I captured today and tell me what needs doing.
steps: Find the notes I saved today.
Read those notes in full with get_note.
Pick out anything in them that is actually an action, rather than a thought I wrote down.
Set a reminder with set_reminder for each action that has a time in it, putting the time in `when` in my own words.
Give me the rest as a short list of what is still open.

skills.name: Draft an email
skills.description: A clear first draft you can edit.
skills.prompt: Draft an email to {{to}} about {{about}}.
steps: Check my notes for anything about {{about}} or {{to}} that the email should take into account.
Write the draft: a clear subject line, a short opening, the point, and a plain closing. Friendly, not formal.

skills.name: Brainstorm ideas
skills.description: A varied list, drawing on your notes.
skills.prompt: Brainstorm ideas about {{topic}} with me.
steps: Look for anything in my notes about {{topic}}, so the ideas build on what I already think.
Give me a varied list of ideas, some obvious, some not, and say which one you would start with.

skills.name: Explain a concept
skills.description: Plain English, with an example.
skills.prompt: Explain {{concept}} to me clearly and simply.
steps: Check whether I already have notes on {{concept}}.
Explain it in plain English with one short example, pitched at what those notes show I already know.
Offer to save the explanation as a note.

skills.name: Create a study plan
skills.description: A realistic plan, with reminders set.
skills.prompt: Help me plan how to get {{goal}} done by {{deadline}}.
steps: Check my notes for anything already written about {{goal}}.
Check the current time with get_current_time, so the dates you work out are real ones.
Lay out a realistic step-by-step plan between now and {{deadline}}.
Set a reminder for the first milestone with set_reminder, and ask before setting the rest.

skills.name: Interview me about an idea
skills.description: Asks you questions to draw out your own thinking, then saves it as a note, not the AI's take on the topic, yours.
skills.when_to_use: when an idea is still half-formed and you want to think it through out loud, not be handed a generic explanation
skills.prompt: Interview me about {{topic}}: ask me questions rather than explaining it back to me.
steps: Check whether I already have notes on {{topic}}, so you don't ask me to repeat what I've already written down.
Ask me one open question about {{topic}}: what's prompting it, or what I already think, and wait for my answer before asking anything else.
Ask 2-3 more questions, one at a time, each building on what I just said rather than a fixed list, the kind a good interviewer asks to get specifics instead of generalities.
Reflect back what you've understood, in my own words and phrasing where you can, and ask me to correct anything that's off before going further.
Write it up as a note: my thinking, in the order it came out, not a generic explanation of {{topic}} and not your own opinions on it. Ask before saving.

skills.name: Build a skill
skills.description: Interviews you about a job you do often, then saves it as a real skill, with steps and an actual tool allowlist, not just a saved sentence.
skills.when_to_use: when something you keep asking the AI to do by hand should become a one-click skill instead
skills.prompt: Help me turn {{task}} into a saved skill.
steps: Call list_skills first: {{task}} may already be close to one that exists, and a near-duplicate is worse than refining the one that's there.
Ask what {{task}} should actually do, step by step, in the order they'd do it themselves, one question, wait for the answer, rather than a checklist dumped at once.
Ask whether it should ever change their notes (create, edit, tag, delete, set reminders) or only read and answer, this decides the tool allowlist.
Ask if any part of it should be a fill-in-the-blank each time it runs (a topic, a deadline, a tag) rather than fixed, that becomes the skill's inputs.
Draft the name, prompt, ordered steps, the specific tools each step needs (nothing broader), and when_to_use, then show the draft and ask before saving anything.
Save it with save_skill once they confirm, using exactly the steps and tools agreed, not a paraphrase.

skills.name: weekly review
skills.prompt: Summarise the week's notes
steps: summarize_notes

result.note_to_model: Built-in skills can be run but not edited. A skill's steps and tools are what it does, copy that shape when you make one. `when_to_use` says when a skill applies; `changes_notes` says whether running it would alter the notebook. Start one with run_skill, passing its name exactly as written here and values for any `inputs`, that ends your turn and the run takes over. Only start one that matches what was asked; a skill that changes notes is not the way to answer a question.
